items.title: A canonical isomorphism between the determinant of the middle term of a short exact sequence of finite projective modules and the tensor product of the outer determinants
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)

items.difficulty_reason: The statement asks for a canonical isomorphism det(M') tensor det(M'') -> det(M) attached to a short exact sequence of finite projective R-modules (source lines 36282-36293). The difficulty is not in finding a map but in making it canonical: the proof first decomposes R into a product of rings indexed by the rank pairs (i, j) of the two outer modules, so that the ranks become constant (proof lines 36296-36301), and then has to produce a map between exterior powers that does not depend on the choices made. The construction uses chosen elements m'_1, ..., m'_i of M' and lifts m_{i+1}, ..., m_{i+j} of chosen elements of M'' (proof lines 36306-36316); the well-definedness and bijectivity of that rule is exactly the part the author states is omitted, and it is the substantive content of the lemma.
